transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. Like, I’ll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers, and then... I just end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and whatever snacks I packed for my classroom.
During these episodes when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you can’t stop or control yourself once you start?

Yeah, that is exactly it. Once I start, um... it feels like the reasonable teacher part of me is just watching from the outside, saying, 'Joan, stop.' But I can't. My hands just keep opening packages and putting food in my mouth, and I just can't stop until I’m painfully full.
After these episodes where you feel out of control with eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or try to compensate in any way for what you’ve eaten?

I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives, no. But I do try to make up for it in other ways. After one of those nights, I’ll tell myself I’m just not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And then... I’ll usually stay out on the trail for hours, or I'll force myself to do extra yoga, even when I’m feeling completely shaky and exhausted. I just feel like I have to do something to fix it.
Do these episodes of eating make you feel very distressed, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yes, they do. It's... it's incredibly distressing. Honestly, my whole life outside of the classroom feels like it revolves around this now. My evenings and weekends are just planned around either the eating or trying to undo what happened. Because of that, I’ve been falling behind on grading papers, which stresses me out even more. I'm definitely less present with my friends because I'm either too exhausted from the exercise or just preoccupied with my eating rules. And at work... I'm just constantly worried about keeping up appearances and seeming like I have it all together for the kids and the other teachers, when really I'm just exhausted and overwhelmed by all of this.
How often do these episodes of uncontrolled eating happen? Are they happening at least once a week?

Yes, definitely at least once a week. Um... for the past few months, honestly, there has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to. And then, the next day, I always try to make up for it by not eating at school, or by pushing myself through a really long walk or extra yoga.

When these episodes happen, does the eating take place all in one go, like within a short period of time—say, a couple of hours—or does it feel more like a longer period where you're just continuously snacking throughout the night?

It's pretty much all in one go, usually within just a couple of hours. I'll start with my dinner leftovers after I finish grading papers for the night, but then... I just keep going. I end up eating an amount of food that honestly scares me. I'll go right from the leftovers into bowls of cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and eventually I'm even going through whatever snacks I had packed for my classroom. So it all happens pretty fast, rather than just grazing or snacking spread out over the whole night.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're completely unable to stop eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah, I do. Once I start, it feels like... well, like the reasonable teacher part of me is just watching from the outside, telling me, Joan, stop. But my hands just keep opening things and putting food in my mouth. I just keep going until I'm painfully full, and I really can't seem to stop myself even when I want to.
Can you tell me if these episodes happen even when you’re not feeling particularly hungry, and if so, do they continue even after you feel physically uncomfortable or in pain?

Yeah, they definitely happen even when I'm not hungry. Usually, I've already eaten dinner, so I'm not actually hungry when it starts. And... yes, I keep eating even after I feel uncomfortable. I'll eat until my stomach physically hurts, until I'm so full it's actually painful, but I still can't stop until everything is just... gone.
Do you feel intense shame, guilt, or disgust with yourself specifically about your eating behaviors during these episodes?

I'm not really sure. I don't think I feel intense shame or disgust, honestly. I mean... I know it's a lot of food, but I haven't really noticed feeling guilty about the eating itself. It's more just that I feel really physically uncomfortable afterwards, rather than being disgusted with myself.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, especially in relation to these eating episodes?

No, I haven't really been feeling down or hopeless. I still enjoy my job and seeing my friends and all of that. I haven't noticed any kind of depression or loss of interest in things, even with the eating episodes going on. It's just the eating itself that's the issue.
When you engage in extra exercise or restrict your eating after these episodes, do you feel like you can’t control those behaviors either, or do you feel more in control during that part?

Um, I'm not really sure how to answer that. I don't really think about it in terms of being in control or out of control. I mean, I just do it because I feel like I have to after eating so much. I haven't really stopped to consider if I could just... not do it. It's just what happens next.
Do you only end up fasting or doing extra exercise after these big eating episodes, or do you also do those things even when you haven’t eaten a lot?

I think it's mostly just... after those big episodes. I haven't really noticed myself fasting or going out of my way to exercise a ton on days where I just eat normally. It pretty much just happens when I feel like I've eaten way too much.
Do you feel upset, anxious, or emotionally overwhelmed specifically while you're going through one of these eating episodes, like when you're actually in the middle of not being able to stop eating?

Um, no, I don't think so. While I'm actually in the middle of it... I don't really feel upset or anxious. It's more like I just zone out completely. I'm not really feeling much of anything right in that moment. The panic and feeling overwhelmed, that really only hits me afterward, once I realize how much I've eaten. But during it, no.
When you fast or do extra exercise after these eating episodes, do you feel any emotional distress, like anxiety or guilt, while you're doing it?

Um, I don't really think so. When I'm fasting or, you know, doing the extra exercise, it's more like I'm just trying to fix what I did. I don't think I feel anxious or guilty *while* I'm doing it. It's almost like a relief, I guess? Like I'm doing what I'm supposed to do to make up for it. The guilt is mostly just right after the eating part.
